summary:
I built the viewer at /score/:id: the score on a paper card, a floating glass player, and a settings sheet with Reproducción, Partitura and Filtros tabs that rebuilds the score as you change settings.
- Score: abcjs renders into a padding-free target with responsive 'resize', paddingright 10 and ink in currentColor. Light and dark therefore switch without re-rendering. Note names use --ink-2. Bars per line come from suggestMeasuresPerLine(score, width, { noteNames, zoom }): 2 at 390 px, 3 at 480 px. Zoom changes staffwidth.
- Cursor: the notes that are sounding light up with --score-highlight, a held bass stays lit while the melody moves, and a soft accent band sits behind the current beat. Taps seek: the nearest note within 36 px. abcjs's own click selection painted tapped notes red, so it is neutralized with selectionColor.
- Follow: when a new system starts and the next one is not visible, the page scrolls the current system to the top. The cursor never hides behind the player.
- Player: elapsed and total time (shown at the current speed), a seekable progress bar, previous and next measure, a big accent play/pause, and quick toggles for metronome, loop (No, Todo, A–B), speed (accent when not 1×) and settings.
- Playback engine: abcjs CreateSynth renders the tune into one AudioBuffer using the offline soundfont (soundFontVolumeMultiplier 3). The metronome and count-in are abcjs drum options with METRONOME_DRUM, drumBars 1, drumIntro 1, and drumOff when only the count-in is on. I then play that buffer myself with AudioBufferSourceNodes. That gives:
  - loops that wrap exactly (loopStart/loopEnd) for Todo and for A–B, picked by tapping two measures and shaded on the score;
  - a cursor clock from the AudioContext minus the output latency;
  - instant seeks.
- Speed 50–150 %, the metronome and the count-in are part of the rendered buffer: changing them during playback re-renders it and carries on from the same spot. Param or ABC changes stop playback cleanly.
- The count-in leads into the start of the current measure.
- The AudioContext is created on the first Play (32 kHz to save memory) and closed on unmount, with window.abcjsAudioContext cleared. Pitches outside 21..109 are dropped from the playback ABC (normally a no-op).
- 'Original' sound appears when the item has audio. It plays the stored recording through an HTMLAudioElement with playbackRate = speed and preservesPitch, starting from score.startSeconds; negative values are clamped. The cursor follows its currentTime.
- Live rebuild: params live in local state. buildScore runs after a 120 ms debounce, and params plus summarizeScore are saved after 600 ms, with any pending save flushed on unmount.
- 'Restablecer' in Filtros resets all params. Demos go back exactly to the seed: { ...demoParams, quantize: 16, difficulty: 'original' }. Other items use defaultParams(analysis, settings).
- When the filters leave no notes, the paper shows a calm message with 'Restablecer filtros', which resets only the filter fields.
- Zoom, hands, speed, loop and sound are remembered per item in localStorage.
- Header: back, a single-line title, a favorite heart (filled in accent, updatedAt not bumped) and an overflow menu: Renombrar, Exportar PDF, MusicXML, MIDI, ABC, Compartir, Duplicar and Eliminar (confirmed, then back to /library). The meta line 'Sol mayor · 4/4 · 100 ppm' opens the Partitura tab.
- PDF: a print-only sheet in black ink with title and composer, one SVG per system with page breaks between systems and balanced systems (16 bars print as 4×4), then window.print().
- MusicXML, MIDI and ABC reuse the library's tested exportFile with the viewer's current params. Toasts use the same wording as the library.
- Also: loading and not-found states, keyboard shortcuts (space, arrows), a screen wake lock while playing, and a 320 px layout. abcjs is loaded on demand in its own chunk (509 KB), outside the main bundle.
Lead note from the library agent: (1) the demo reset now matches the seed (quantize 16). (2) Exports reuse exportFile. (3) The viewer does not use useNavigationType, so no impact. (4) My test seeding copes with the real seed.
Client feedback: docs/CLIENT-FEEDBACK.md had no entries at the start or the end, so there was nothing to apply.
public_api_notes:
ROUTE: '/score/:id' -> ViewerScreen (same export and path).
SELECTORS (for the integration e2e):
- Score: .vw-paper svg. Notes: .vw-paper .abcjs-note (abcjs groups with classes abcjs-mm<measure> abcjs-v<0 RH|1 LH> abcjs-n<i>). Playing notes: .vw-paper .vw-on. Cursor band: .vw-cursor. A–B band: .vw-band.
- Player: .vw-player[data-status=idle|loading|countin|playing|paused]. Play: .vw-player__playbtn (aria-label Reproducir / Pausar). Progress: .vw-player__slider input, value in score seconds. Total: .vw-player__time--total. Speed label: .vw-player__speed.
- Buttons: button[aria-label="Compás anterior"], ["Compás siguiente"], ["Metrónomo"], ["Ajustes de la partitura"]. The loop button is .vw-player__loop .ui-iconbtn and cycles No -> Todo -> A–B.
- Header: meta line .vw-meta ('Sol mayor · 4/4 · 100 ppm'; after transposing +2 it reads 'La mayor · …'). Favorite .vw-fav (aria-pressed). Overflow: button[aria-label="Más opciones"] -> .ui-actionsheet__item, found by label text.
- Sheet: .vw-sheet with tabs .vw-sheet__tabs .ui-seg__item [Reproducción, Partitura, Filtros]. Find rows by .ui-row__title text. Transponer: .ui-stepper__btn[aria-label="Aumentar"]. Manos 'Derecha' leaves one staff per system: .abcjs-staff-wrapper.abcjs-l0 .abcjs-staff count = 1. Restablecer: .vw-panel__reset .ui-btn.
- No notes left after the filters: .vw-empty, with the button 'Restablecer filtros'.
- Print sheet: .vw-print, a child of body, removed after printing. To test the PDF headless, override window.print before choosing 'Exportar PDF'.
STATE:
- localStorage 'pauta.viewer.<id>' = {zoom, hands, speed, loop: 'off'|'all'|'ab', loopRange: [a, b] | null, sound: 'piano'|'original'}.
- Global settings used: noteNaming, metronome, countIn, followScore, playbackVolume.
- DB writes:
  - updateScore(id, {openedAt}, false) on open;
  - {params, summary} debounced 600 ms (touch true), flushed on unmount;
  - {favorite} with touch false;
  - {title} on rename;
  - duplicateScore / deleteScore from the menu.
AUDIO:
- One AudioContext per viewer, created on the first Play (a user gesture) at 32 kHz with a default fallback. It is registered for abcjs through init({audioContext}), so window.abcjsAudioContext is ours. On unmount it is closed and the global deleted.
- Sound is never started without a gesture. Headless runs therefore only need a click (the --autoplay-policy flag is harmless).
- Score time = tickToSeconds at 100 %. Displayed times are divided by speed.
EXPORTS: src/features/library/exports.ts exportFile({...doc, params: liveParams}, format) + shareOrDownload, so file names and MIME types match the library. Toasts: '<MusicXML|MIDI|ABC> descargado', 'Partitura compartida', 'Partitura duplicada', 'Partitura eliminada'. PDF: printScore() in src/features/viewer/exports.ts.
GOTCHA (anyone rendering abcjs interactively): abcjs always attaches click selection and paints the clicked note #ff0000 unless renderAbc gets selectionColor (the viewer passes 'currentColor'). Also, abcjs measures with getBBox, so never render into a display:none container. The print sheet is laid out off-screen with visibility: hidden for that reason.

requests.request: In scripts/e2e.mjs, use the viewer selectors from public_api_notes. The playback state is .vw-player[data-status]. The highlight is .vw-paper .vw-on, whose classes change over time; poll the abcjs-mm/abcjs-n classes. For the transpose check, the meta line .vw-meta goes from 'Sol mayor' to 'La mayor' on the Ode. For 'Manos: Derecha', count .abcjs-staff-wrapper.abcjs-l0 .abcjs-staff (expect 1). Override window.print before 'Exportar PDF' so headless Chrome is not blocked.

Optional kit polish, worked around inside the viewer: (a) export useElementWidth from src/ui/index.tsx (the viewer has its own ResizeObserver hook); (b) a `loading` prop on IconButton (the viewer overlays a Spinner on the play button).

docs/CONTINUAR.md section 4: viewer done (phase B). All the VIEWER prompt items and the VIEWER_B requests are implemented. Optional BRIEF note: abcjs is now loaded lazily from the viewer, in its own 509 KB chunk precached by the PWA.

known_issues: abcjs renders the whole tune into one stereo Float32 buffer: about duration/speed × 32 000 Hz × 8 B. That is ~23 MB for 90 s at 1×, and ~150 MB for a 5-minute import at 0.5×. Very long transcriptions at slow speeds may be heavy on low-end phones.

Speed, metronome and count-in are baked into the buffer. Changing them during playback re-renders it (~60–150 ms for the demos, longer for long pieces), so there is a short gap before playback continues from the same spot.
With the count-in on, playback restarts from the beginning of the current measure (the count-in leads into a downbeat), including after a mid-measure pause.

The metronome and count-in only apply to the Piano sound; with 'Original' they are disabled in the sheet and the bar. Original seek and loop accuracy depends on HTMLAudioElement (tens of ms), unlike the sample-exact piano loop.
Original playback with a negative score.startSeconds (pickup) clamps to the start of the recording. The part of the score before the audio begins is skipped (nothing audible there).
No cover -> viewer layoutId transition: the viewer has no cover (the score is the hero), so the page's push slide is used.
The PDF prints what is on screen: the chosen hands and note names. Tap-to-seek has no keyboard equivalent beyond the progress slider and previous/next measure (space and arrows work on desktop).
Verified headless only. The AudioContext runs, buffers render, sources play and positions advance in real time, but I did not listen to the sound on speakers.
